ideas.title: The inventory cap silently triples the reward penalty
ideas.claim: When |inventory| reaches max_inventory_shares the engine zeroes the adding side, leaving a one-sided book that scores max(Q1,Q2)/3 at best and zero outside [0.10, 0.90]; a soft ramp that starts shrinking at 0.6 and pulls at 0.85 keeps the single-sided fraction under 1 % of events instead of the baseline's >= 5 %, without lowering net.
ideas.mechanism: The engine implements the cap as a binary stop (`bid_size = 0 if inv >= max`), which is the correct risk control and the wrong reward control: the venue's Q_min is the minimum of the two book sides, so losing one side loses two-thirds of the score, and near the price boundaries it loses all of it. The maker therefore pays a discrete reward cliff for a marginal risk reduction that a size ramp delivers smoothly. The pool underpays the capped maker relative to the ramped one at identical average inventory. This is a control-shape mechanism, not a risk-premium or signal mechanism.
ideas.data: DecisionContext only: inventory_shares, max_inventory_shares, mid, spread_cents. No derived table, no clock.
ideas.module: ideas.micro-cap-breadth-preserve.module
ideas.metric: Fraction of events with a single-sided book (one side size 0) and the paired per-condition net; the deciding number is the paired net delta per share with the single-sided fraction as the mechanism check.
ideas.kill: Kill if the baseline's single-sided fraction is below 1 % of events (nothing to fix), or if peak |inventory| rises by more than 10 % under the ramp, or if paired net is not positive on both slices.
ideas.author: IdeaGenMicro

ideas.title: Share is concave in size and linear in competition
ideas.claim: Since our pool share is S/(S + C), once the qualifying band already holds competition C worth >= 4x our full-size score, extra size buys less than 20 % of that size in share; sizing to a fixed 25 % target share instead of quoting full size cuts fill_notional by >= 30 % on the most crowded tercile of conditions while losing <= 10 % of rewards_usd.
ideas.mechanism: The pool pays Q_normal = Q_min / sum(Q_min across makers) each minute (Polymarket docs, eq. 5), so the marginal dollar of reward per marginal share falls as C/(S + C)^2 while the adverse-selection cost per share is constant. The venue's own competing score is not in our DecisionContext today, so the market-maker who ignores C over-sizes exactly where the reward is already crowded and under-sizes where the pool is uncontested. The pool underpays marginal size; the counterparty is whoever is willing to sweep a large resting quote. This is a competition-elasticity mechanism, not a fill-probability or flow mechanism.
ideas.data: clob_events + the universe snapshot, resolved to per-(asset, second) band competition. prepare.sql materialises data/derived/ideas/micro-competition-dilution/comp_score.parquet with columns (asset_id, ts_second, comp_score, band_depth_shares, band_depth_usd), where comp_score is sum over levels with 0 <= (mid - price)*100 <= rewards_max_spread of ((v - s)/v)^2 * size, mirroring compute_competing_depth_score; the harness then injects ctx.signals["comp_score"].
ideas.module: ideas.micro-competition-dilution.module
ideas.metric: Paired per-condition net and fill_notional in the top competition tercile, with rewards_usd reported alongside; deciding number is the paired net difference against queue_aware_ofi with the fill reduction as the mechanism check.
ideas.kill: Kill if comp_score varies by less than 5x across the sample (nothing to dilute), or if the reward loss exceeds twice the fill-notional saving on both slices, or if the top tercile contributes more than 25 % of the total (concentration gate).
ideas.author: IdeaGenMicro

ideas.title: Substitute the sibling token instead of dropping a side
ideas.claim: When protection says pull one side of token A, moving that size to the complementary token B on the same Q side (Q1 = YES bid + NO ask) keeps Q_min within 10 % of the fully two-sided baseline while still removing the threatened exposure, improving paired net by >= $0.001/share over a per-side pull.
ideas.mechanism: The official score pairs YES bids with NO asks into Q1 and YES asks with NO bids into Q2, then takes max(min(Q1,Q2), max(Q1,Q2)/3) inside the mid band (Polymarket docs, eqs. 2-4). Our two tokens are one condition, so the harness gives one strategy instance both books; a maker who drops A's threatened ask loses Q2's contribution while the economically equivalent exposure on B is untouched and could carry the score. The pool underpays the maker who thinks per token instead of per Q side, and the counterparty is the taker on the side we abandoned. This is a pairing/eligibility mechanism: the signal is unchanged, only where the size lives changes.
ideas.data: DecisionContext for both assets of the condition (available because setup binds one module instance per condition and the harness calls decide for each token), plus MarketView.tokens. No derived table.
ideas.module: ideas.micro-cross-token-substitution.module
ideas.metric: Condition-level paired net versus queue_aware_ofi, plus a condition-level two-sidedness proxy (both Q sides non-zero at the epoch sample, computed from the per-token epoch snapshots); deciding number is the paired net delta with the two-sidedness change printed beside it. Caveat: the engine scores each token additively with no Q1/Q2 min, so the proxy and not rewards_usd is the falsifying number until rewards.compute_epoch_payout is patched.
ideas.kill: Kill if the two-sidedness fraction improves by less than 20 percentage points, or if condition-level inventory variance rises by more than 10 %, or if paired net is not positive on both slices.
ideas.author: IdeaGenMicro

ideas.title: Resting depth imbalance is the stock version of OFI
ideas.claim: The instantaneous imbalance between bid-side and ask-side size at the touch, |(bid_size - ask_size)| / (bid_size + ask_size) >= 0.5, identifies the threatened side at the very next book update with >= 60 % hit rate, versus ~55 % for the trailing 60 s OFI sign, and gating on it improves paired net by >= $0.001/share.
ideas.mechanism: OFI is a *flow* average over a trailing window: it needs history and lags every repricing. The two level sizes in our context are a *stock*: they say which side of the book is thin right now, and a thin side is the one a sweep reaches first - the same depth logic that makes price impact inversely proportional to depth (Cont, Kukanov & Stoikov 2014). The two are not substitutes: a book can have zero net flow and still be lopsided because one side's resting size was never replenished. The counterparty is the taker who arrives into the thin side while our quote sits on it. No fill model and no queue position is used.
ideas.data: DecisionContext only: bid_size_at_level, ask_size_at_level, mid, best_bid, best_ask, spread_cents. No derived table, no clock.
ideas.module: ideas.micro-depth-imbalance.module
ideas.metric: Next-update hit rate of the predicted threatened side (does that side's best price worsen or does its level shrink?) and the paired per-condition net; the deciding number is the paired net delta per share against queue_aware_ofi.
ideas.kill: Kill if the hit rate is below 55 %, or if the resulting markout gap between quoted and shrunk sides is below 0.3 c/share, or if the paired net delta is not positive on both slices.
ideas.author: IdeaGenMicro

ideas.title: Terminal jumps are the only risk that never mean-reverts
ideas.claim: Fills in the last 60 minutes before a market's end_date carry markout at least 2x worse than the same market's earlier fills, and flattening (min size, no adding) in the final 6 hours with a full pull in the final hour improves paired net by >= $0.002/share on non-sentinel markets.
ideas.mechanism: A binary mid near expiry is a martingale that can jump to 0 or 1 on a single news item, so the inventory term is bounded above by the distance to the boundary while the reward term does not grow at all; Avellaneda-Stoikov's (T-t) term goes to zero, meaning the inventory penalty per unit time is largest exactly when the remaining time is shortest - but the size that carries it should shrink, and the engine has no expiry input. The counterparty is the informed trader who knows the outcome before the mid does. The repo's own caveat applies: end_date is not resolution time (median end_date to resolved_ts is +4 h, p10 -133 h), so the rule is deliberately one-sided (flatten early, never last-minute).
ideas.data: Universe snapshot end_date/slug plus clob_events for the market's own tape; prepare.sql materialises data/derived/ideas/micro-expiry-flatten/ttr.parquet with (asset_id, hour_utc, ttr_seconds, is_sentinel) joining the universe manifest to the tape's asset list, and the harness injects signals["ttr_seconds"].
ideas.module: ideas.micro-expiry-flatten.module
ideas.metric: Paired per-condition net, with the markout of final-hour fills versus the same condition's earlier fills as the mechanism check, and rewards_usd reported as the forfeited term; the deciding number is the paired net delta per share.
ideas.kill: Kill if the final-hour markout is within 0.5 c/share of the same market's earlier markout, or if the end_date-to-resolution error makes the window fire in fewer than 20 conditions, or if reward loss exceeds the markout saving on both slices.
ideas.author: IdeaGenMicro

ideas.title: A fill that flattens us is worth more than its markout
ideas.claim: The toxicity gate is inventory-blind: at the same signal strength, a fill that reduces |inventory| is worth at least 0.5 c/share more *net* (markout plus rebalance value) than a fill that increases it, so suppressing the pull when the threatened side is the reducing side improves paired net by >= $0.001/share over queue_aware_ofi at equal or lower risk.
ideas.mechanism: Inventory has a shadow price: being long makes a sell fill worth markout plus the release of the inventory penalty (the q*gamma*sigma^2 term in Avellaneda-Stoikov), and being short makes a buy fill symmetric. The existing gate decides per side from flow alone and therefore defends the reducing side as hard as the adding side, which throws away the cheapest flattening opportunities exactly when inventory is largest. The counterparty on a reducing fill is a taker buying our inventory at a price that already includes a spread we were paid to hold. This is the interaction of the risk term with the signal, not a new signal and not a size rule.
ideas.data: DecisionContext only: inventory_shares, max_inventory_shares, ofi, queue ratios, sizes. No derived table, no clock.
ideas.module: ideas.micro-gate-inventory-interaction.module
ideas.metric: Paired per-condition net against queue_aware_ofi, with the markout of reducing fills versus adding fills at matched signal strength as the mechanism check, and peak |inventory| as the risk check.
ideas.kill: Kill if the reducing-versus-adding net gap is below 0.2 c/share, or if peak |inventory| rises by more than 15 %, or if paired net is not positive on both slices.
ideas.author: IdeaGenMicro

ideas.title: Skew the size, not the price
ideas.claim: Because the engine's price skew is capped at 0.5 c and moves both quotes (pushing one of them out of the reward band), size skewing the side that increases |inventory| cuts peak |inventory| by >= 30 % and inventory_mtm variance by >= 25 % with a reward loss under 5 %, giving a paired net at least as good as the baseline.
ideas.mechanism: Inventory risk is q * sigma * sqrt(horizon); the standard response is a reservation-price shift (Avellaneda-Stoikov), which this engine already implements as a 0.5 c cap. But that cap is small relative to a 1 c tick, so at high inventory the price skew either does nothing or pushes the adding side's quote a full tick farther from mid, cutting its score by more than it cuts its fill probability. Shifting *size* instead leaves both quotes at their scored distance and simply stops adding to the position, which is the same risk reduction with no score penalty. The pool underpays price-skewed quotes at 1 c ticks; the counterparty is the informed taker who fills the adding side while we are already long.
ideas.data: DecisionContext only: inventory_shares, max_inventory_shares, mid, spread_cents. No derived table, no clock.
ideas.module: ideas.micro-inventory-skew-size.module
ideas.metric: Paired per-condition net (cash_pnl + inventory_mtm + rewards_usd) against reactionary, with peak |inventory| and inventory_mtm standard deviation reported as the mechanism check, and rewards_usd as the cost.
ideas.kill: Kill if peak |inventory| falls by less than 15 %, or if rewards_usd falls by more than 10 %, or if paired net is not positive on both slices.
ideas.author: IdeaGenMicro

ideas.title: The queue ratio is only defined when we join a level
ideas.claim: The FIFO queue ratio is degenerate in the regimes where the engine creates a new price level: a joined level starts at ratio 1.0 (level size ahead of us), an empty new level starts at 0.0, and the ratio only becomes informative as our own level accumulates size; therefore the queue-aware gate's measured gain comes from the join regime, and applying it outside that regime adds decisions without information - the join-regime paired net delta is at least 1.5x the all-regime delta.
ideas.mechanism: The paper engine replays FIFO per quote as q_ahead = displayed level size at our price when we join, with arrivals behind us growing q_behind (engine._update_level_queue). The engine prices at mid +- max(0.2 c, 0.75 c) and post-only clamps; with a 1 c tick that places us one tick off mid, which coincides with the best bid/ask only when the spread is about two ticks. In a one-tick book we are one tick behind the touch (an empty new level, ratio 0) and in a three-tick-or-wider book we are alone inside the spread (also a fresh level, ratio 0); in both we are structurally "front of queue" no matter what the flow does, so the 0.60 threshold cannot fire and the gate is inert. Only in the join case does the measured +0.00364 $/share front versus -0.02014 $/share back split apply. The pool pays the same either way, so the distinction is about where protection is real.
ideas.data: DecisionContext only: spread_cents, tick_size, best_bid, best_ask, mid, bid_queue_ratio, ask_queue_ratio, bid_size_at_level, ask_size_at_level. No derived table, no clock.
ideas.module: ideas.micro-join-vs-lead.module
ideas.metric: Paired per-condition net against queue_aware_ofi computed separately on the join and non-join subsets, plus the fraction of updates per regime; the deciding number is the join-regime paired delta, with the non-join subset required not to degrade.
ideas.kill: Kill if the join regime is under 10 % of updates, or if the join-regime paired delta is not at least 1.5x the all-regime delta, or if the non-join subset degrades by more than $0.001/share on either slice.
ideas.author: IdeaGenMicro

ideas.title: Pull on the jump, not after it
ideas.claim: A >= 2-tick mid move inside <= 3 book events identifies an information arrival; quotes that stay resting through the following 5 events are filled at markout 1.0 c/share worse than quotes pulled for those 5 events, and a jump-triggered withdrawal improves paired net by >= $0.001/share while costing < 5 % of reward time.
ideas.mechanism: The tape is event-driven, so a two-tick repricing in three events is not drift, it is someone acting on news; the counterparty takes the stale side of every quote left behind, and our cancel path upper bound (217.5 ms measured CLOB minimum RTT) is shorter than the taker's round trip, which is why the repo's Binance lead is defensive rather than directional. The measured asymmetry is that the engine re-prices on the next book update anyway, so the only decision left is whether to be present in the gap; the OFI gate's 60 s trailing mean cannot see a jump until it is over. This is information arrival, distinct from bounce and from queue state.
ideas.data: DecisionContext only: book.mid and best_bid/best_ask per update; the module keeps the previous mid and a small event counter. No derived table, no clock.
ideas.module: ideas/micro-jump-withdrawal/module.py
ideas.metric: Paired per-condition net, with the markout of fills within 5 events of a jump versus fills outside such windows as the mechanism check, and time_quoted_frac as the reward cost.
ideas.kill: Kill if the in-window fill markout is not worse by 0.3 c/share, or if jumps occur in fewer than 2 % of updates (too rare to matter), or if the reward forfeiture exceeds the markout saving on both slices.
ideas.author: IdeaGenMicro

ideas.title: YES plus NO is one dollar, so inventory is a sum, not two positions
ideas.claim: Because a filled YES bid plus a filled NO bid at a combined price below $1 is a riskless $1 claim, the true inventory is the pair, not each token; sizing into the cheap complement when mid_YES + mid_NO <= 0.99 completes >= 10 % of pairs and adds >= $0.005/share of carry with no additional inventory risk, improving paired net per condition.
ideas.mechanism: The two tokens of one condition are claims on the same $1: buying both for 0.98 locks 0.02, and the repo already merges them (src/polymarketbot/rewards/merger.py). The engine, however, tracks positions per token and halts each side at max_inventory_shares independently, so a maker who is long YES is treated as having no NO exposure and is stopped from completing the pair exactly when completing it would remove all risk. The pool pays for both quotes meanwhile. The counterparty is the taker who sells each leg separately and does not net them. This is complement arithmetic, distinct from any per-token inventory rule.
ideas.data: DecisionContext for both tokens (one module instance per condition) plus MarketView.tokens; the module reads mid_YES and mid_NO from the two books it already receives. No derived table.
ideas.module: ideas.micro-net-complement-inventory.module
ideas.metric: Pair-completion rate (fraction of conditions where both legs fill within the slice) and the paired per-condition net; the deciding number is the net delta per share against reactionary, with inventory_mtm variance reported as the risk check.
ideas.kill: Kill if pair completion is below 10 % of conditions, or if the realised carry per completed pair is below $0.002/share, or if condition-level inventory variance rises by more than 10 % on both slices.
ideas.author: IdeaGenMicro

ideas.title: Bid-ask bounce is noise; same-sign runs are information
ideas.claim: Updates whose mid changes alternate sign (flip fraction >= 0.7 over the last 30 changes) carry markout of +0.2 c/share or better, while low-flip updates (<= 0.3) carry -1.0 c/share or worse; conditioning quote size on that flip fraction improves paired net by >= $0.001/share versus the queue gate.
ideas.mechanism: A top-of-book that oscillates between two prices with no direction is the classic bid-ask bounce: trades hit alternating sides and the mid returns, so a resting maker is paid the spread and nothing informative is happening. A top that steps in one direction is real information being repriced one tick at a time, and every quote on the wrong side of that path is stale. The distinction is in the *sign pattern* of mid changes, not their magnitude and not the signed mean the OFI gate uses; a choppy but symmetric book has OFI near zero yet is the worst state for a maker, while a one-way drift has a large OFI that the gate catches late. The counterparty is the taker who is repricing, not the one who is bouncing.
ideas.data: DecisionContext only: each decide carries book.mid; the module keeps the last 30 distinct mid values and derives the sign of each change, then flip_frac = share of consecutive pairs with opposite signs. No derived table, no clock.
ideas.module: ideas.micro-oscillation-vs-trend.module
ideas.metric: Markout ladder across flip_frac terciles (the mechanism check) and the paired per-condition net against queue_aware_ofi; deciding number is the paired net delta per share.
ideas.kill: Kill if the tercile markout spread is below 0.3 c/share, or if the high-flip tercile is not the better one, or if the paired net delta is not positive on both slices.
ideas.author: IdeaGenMicro

ideas.title: The $1 floor makes small-share markets a zero-reward game
ideas.claim: At least 15 % of the rewarded universe projects a daily payout below the venue's $1 minimum at min-size quoting, so on those conditions the reward term is exactly zero and quoting both sides is pure adverse selection; pulling them removes their fills with zero reward loss and improves paired net by >= $0.001/share.
ideas.mechanism: The venue pays only if the day's total exceeds $1 (docs: "The minimum reward payout is $1"). A median market here has rate_per_day = $33 and min_size = 20 shares, so our score fraction must exceed 3 % of the pool for the day to pay anything at all; with full depth in the band from larger makers that fraction can sit below the floor for the whole day. In that state the entire reward channel is dead and the only remaining term is the fill markout, which the repo measures at -0.00628 $/share for the unconditional both-sides quote. The counterparty is the taker who knows the reward is not compensating us.
ideas.data: Universe snapshot (daily_pool, min_size, max_spread) + clob_events for competing band depth. prepare.sql materialises data/derived/ideas/micro-payout-floor/proj_payout.parquet with (condition_id, asset_id, date, comp_score_median, our_min_size_score, proj_daily_usd_at_min, proj_daily_usd_at_full); proj_daily_usd = rate_per_day * S_ours/(S_ours + comp_score_median). Harness injects signals["proj_daily_usd_at_full"].
ideas.module: ideas.micro-payout-floor.module
ideas.metric: Fraction of rewarded conditions projected below the floor, and the paired net difference on that subset; the deciding number is the paired net delta per share on below-floor conditions with the rewards_usd delta printed next to it.
ideas.kill: Kill if fewer than 5 % of rewarded conditions fall below the floor, or if below-floor conditions show reactionary markout >= +0.001 $/share (i.e. they are profitable to quote anyway), or if the projection's error versus realised epoch payouts exceeds 2x on the calibration slice.
ideas.author: IdeaGenMicro

ideas.title: Fills beget fills: defend after our own fill, not only ahead of it
ideas.claim: The 10 book events after one of our own fills carry at least 1.5x the adverse markout of the same market's steady state, so a post-fill defensive window on the filled side (and on both sides if the mid has moved in the fill's direction) improves markout_5m_bps by >= 0.3 c/share at matched fill count.
ideas.mechanism: A fill on our bid means a seller crossed into us; if that seller is the first slice of an informed order, the same information keeps arriving, and the quotes we leave behind are the next slices in line. This is continuation, not prediction: the module reacts to its own execution, which is the one event the venue gives us for free and which no price-only signal encodes. The measured markout here is -0.02014 $/share for back-of-queue fills on 281 observations, which is consistent with fills clustering inside informed episodes. The counterparty is the informed taker's second and third slice. Distinct from the OFI gate, which needs a trailing 60 s price window and never looks at our executions.
ideas.data: Context plus the on_trade hook (price, size, side). Our own fill is identified by a print at or through our resting quote price on the matching side, which decide can reconstruct from the previous best_bid/best_ask it observed. No derived table.
ideas.module: ideas.micro-post-fill-defence.module
ideas.metric: Paired per-condition net with markout_5m_bps as the primary mechanism number; deciding statistic is the paired markout improvement on post-fill fills, with net required to be positive too.
ideas.kill: Kill if post-fill markout is not worse than pre-fill by 0.3 c/share pooled across conditions, or if the module's fill count falls below 200 on both slices.
ideas.author: IdeaGenMicro

ideas.title: A print that clears half the level is a sweep, not noise
ideas.claim: Prints whose size is at least half of the displayed level size identify in-progress sweeps: they occur in >= 5 % of prints and the fill markout in the following 10 events is at least 1.5x worse than after small prints, so shrinking on them improves paired net by >= $0.001/share while the absolute-size threshold that failed before stays out of the rule.
ideas.mechanism: The repo's live size-weighted gate (850 shares / 1.5 c) failed because a fixed share count means nothing across markets with 20-share and 1,000-share minimums; the same print is enormous in one market and trivial in another. Size *relative to the level it just consumed* is scale-free and says whether the trade ate the queue (informed aggression, likely to continue into the next level) or nibbled it (noise). The trailing price-only OFI mean cannot see this because it ignores print size and needs 60 s of history. The counterparty is the aggressor's next slice, which arrives before the next book update settles. This conditions on prints, not on our own fill (that is micro-post-fill-defence) and not on queue position.
ideas.data: The on_trade hook (price, size, side) plus the last observed bid_size_at_level / ask_size_at_level from the context. No derived table, no clock.
ideas.module: ideas.micro-print-sweep-detector.module
ideas.metric: Paired per-condition net against queue_aware_ofi, with the markout of fills inside sweep windows versus outside as the mechanism check, and the median consumed fraction reported so the 0.5 threshold is auditable.
ideas.kill: Kill if sweep prints are under 5 % of prints, or if the in-window markout gap is below 0.3 c/share, or if the rule repeats the 850/1.5 c failure (paired net at or below baseline on both slices).
ideas.author: IdeaGenMicro
ideas.evidence: tape_net vs reactionary on the 70-market liquid universe, --flat 200, synthetic prints: 40 mkts 02:10 +$26.25 (t=2.82); 40 mkts 02:50 +$23.48 (t=2.41); 70 mkts 02:10 +$73.36 (t=1.52). Sign is consistent, significance is not: the 70-market slice is the honest one and it does not clear t>=2.

ideas.title: Overshooting the smaller Q side is a wasted order
ideas.claim: Because Q_min = min(Q1, Q2), every share added to the already-larger Q side earns nothing; after any protective shrink or fill the two Q totals diverge by >= 1.5x in at least 25 % of updates, and equalising them raises rewards_usd by >= 8 % at unchanged fill_notional.
ideas.mechanism: The venue aggregates Q_one = sum of YES bids + NO asks and Q_two = sum of YES asks + NO bids across the market and its complement, then scores Q_min = min(Q1, Q2) inside the band and max(min(Q1,Q2), max(Q1,Q2)/3) inside [0.10, 0.90] (Polymarket docs, eqs. 2-4). Our two tokens quote both sides at the same share size, so the two totals match only while all four orders rest at the same distance; the moment one side is shrunk for protection, or one leg fills, the larger side carries score that is arithmetically discarded. A maker who sizes each side "for safety" therefore buys risk with no reward, and the counterparty fills that overshoot for free. This is the aggregation rule itself - not the single-sided penalty (micro-two-sided-coupling) and not moving a pulled side to the sibling (micro-cross-token-substitution).
ideas.data: DecisionContext for both tokens of the condition (one module instance per condition, decide called per token) plus MarketView.rewards_min_size and rewards_max_spread. The module reconstructs each side's score density from mid/best_bid/best_ask/tick as in micro-score-density-split. No derived table.
ideas.module: ideas.micro-qmin-equalisation.module
ideas.metric: Paired per-condition rewards_usd against reactionary at unchanged fill_notional, with the distribution of Q1/Q2 per update and the fraction of updates outside [0.8, 1.25] reported; the deciding number is the paired reward delta per condition. Caveat the run must respect: paper_trading/rewards.compute_epoch_payout sums per-token bid+ask scores with no Q_min and no c factor, so rewards_usd on today's engine cannot express this claim; the run needs the Q1/Q2 proxy from the per-token epoch snapshots or a scoring patch in rewards.py before this metric can falsify anything.
ideas.kill: Kill if Q1/Q2 stays inside [0.8, 1.25] in 90 % or more of updates (nothing to equalise), or if the paired reward gain is under 3 % on both slices, or if fill_notional rises by more than 5 %.
ideas.author: IdeaGenMicro
ideas.kill_reason: Refuted by the venue formula we now implement: Q_norm = Q_two + min(Q_one, Q_two)/3. When both sides rest, Q_one = 0 and Q_norm = Q_two = the plain sum, so unequal side sizes are NOT penalised. The idea assumed Q_min caps the smaller side inside a two-sided book, which the published rule does not do.

ideas.title: Queue erosion velocity, not queue level
ideas.claim: The rate at which our own queue ratio falls, not its level, predicts the next adverse fill: fills arriving after a >= 0.2 drop in bid/ask queue ratio within 10 events carry markout 1.5 c/share worse than fills at a stable ratio, so shrinking on erosion improves paired net by >= $0.001/share over a level-only threshold.
ideas.mechanism: The queue ratio is q_ahead/(q_ahead + q_behind). A ratio that falls quickly means the size in front of us is disappearing - either cancels (harmless, and the level is being abandoned) or fills (the level is being eaten, and we are next). The level alone cannot tell those apart; velocity can, because a level being eaten moves the whole ladder while cancels typically thin it in place. Moallemi and Yuan value queue position precisely because depth ahead raises the adverse-selection cost of the fill you do receive; a fast-shrinking queue is that cost arriving in real time. The counterparty is the taker already consuming the level ahead of us.
ideas.data: DecisionContext only: bid_queue_ratio, ask_queue_ratio, bid_size_at_level, ask_size_at_level, mid per update; the module keeps a 10-event history per side. No derived table, no clock.
ideas.module: ideas/micro-queue-erosion-velocity/module.py
ideas.metric: Paired per-condition net against queue_aware_ofi, with the eroded-versus-stable markout gap as the mechanism check; the deciding number is the paired net delta per share.
ideas.kill: Kill if the eroded-versus-stable markout gap is below 0.4 c/share, or if fewer than 30 conditions show any >= 0.2 erosion episode, or if the paired net delta is negative on either slice.

ideas.title: Price every pull in forfeited reward dollars
ideas.claim: A pull that is decided on risk alone over-pulls, because reward income is proportional to time-in-band while fills arrive at roughly 1 % per episode; pricing each pull as (forfeited epoch reward) versus (expected fill saving) improves paired net by >= 5 % at the same or lower fill count than the fixed ratio-0.60 gate, while keeping time_quoted_frac above 0.90.
ideas.mechanism: The reward is sampled once per minute at a random offset and summed over the epoch, so being out of the book for a second costs reward in expectation at the full rate, whereas the fill it avoids is a ~1 % event (the repo's backtester measures 0.98 % fills per episode). The existing queue gate spends reward without a price: it compares a queue ratio to 0.60 and never asks whether the saved markout exceeds the forfeited dollars. The pool underpays any gate whose saving is below the reward it discards, and the taker profits from exactly those pulls. No new signal is needed; the mechanism is the unit conversion.
ideas.data: DecisionContext (queue ratios, sizes, inventory, ofi) + MarketView (rate_per_day, rewards_min_size, rewards_max_spread). Priors on markout from docs/predictive-mm-analysis.md (front +0.36 c/share, back -2.01 c/share, baseline -0.628 c/share on 777 marked fills). No derived table.

ideas.metric: Paired per-condition net with rewards_usd, fills and time_quoted_frac reported together; deciding number is net at equal-or-lower fills versus queue_aware_ofi, with the 0.90 time_quoted_frac gate applied.
ideas.kill: Kill if priced and unpriced gates land within $0.001/share on both slices, or if the priced gate needs time_quoted_frac below 0.90 to show its gain, or if the markout prior's error on the calibration hour exceeds 50 % (the conversion would be meaningless).

ideas.title: Score density: the quadratic pays four times more for the same shares at half the distance
ideas.claim: Because S is quadratic in distance and linear in size, inventory skew plus post-only clamping make the two sides of one book differ in reward per share by >= 1.5x in at least 20 % of updates; reallocating size to the higher-density side raises rewards_usd per unit of fill_notional by >= 10 % with unchanged time_quoted_frac.
ideas.mechanism: S = ((v - s)/v)^2 * size, so a side at s = v/2 earns a quarter of the score of a side at s = 0 for identical shares (Polymarket docs). The engine prices both sides from the same mid +- offset but post-only clamping and inventory skew break the symmetry: the clamped side sits materially farther from mid and earns a smaller fraction of its size. The pool therefore underpays the symmetric quote and overpays the asymmetric one; the fix is a size rule, not a signal. This is not the queue gate: no fill probability and no flow enter, only the score geometry.
ideas.data: DecisionContext only: mid, best_bid, best_ask, tick_size, spread_cents, inventory_shares and max_inventory_shares (for the skew term); rewards_max_spread at setup.

ideas.title: Flow on YES threatens the NO bid first
ideas.claim: The two tokens of one condition are anti-correlated, so YES-side order-flow imbalance threatens the NO-side bid before NO's own OFI moves; using the sibling token's OFI (sign-flipped) as an additional threat signal raises the gate's markout improvement by >= 0.2 c/share at the same fill count.
ideas.mechanism: YES and NO must sum to about $1, so a buy program on YES that lifts the YES offer is simultaneously a sell program on NO that hits the NO bid; the NO book lags because its market makers react to their own book, not to the sibling's. A maker who reads both books therefore sees the NO threat one or more events early, in the same way cross-venue leads are used defensively (Kalshi trade flow leads Polymarket by 1 s at 0.696 agreement in this repo's own measurement). The counterparty is the taker working the pair. This uses cross-token flow, not the sibling's price, and not the same-token OFI the baseline already consumes.
ideas.data: DecisionContext for both assets of the condition (one module instance per condition, decide called per token), so the module can record each token's ctx.ofi and observe the sibling's last value. No derived table, no clock.

ideas.metric: Paired per-condition net against queue_aware_ofi, with the lead statistic reported (fraction of threat episodes where the sibling signal fires at least one book update before the own-token signal) and markout_5m_bps as the mechanism check.
ideas.kill: Kill if the sibling leads in fewer than 10 % of threat episodes, or if the added markout improvement is below 0.1 c/share, or if the paired net delta is not positive on both slices.

ideas.title: When the book widens without a move, the makers know something
ideas.claim: A spread widening of >= 2 ticks with no mid change in the same window is followed by fills at markout 1.0 c/share worse than the market's quiet-state fills; pulling both sides for 5 events after such an episode improves paired net by >= $0.001/share and costs less than 5 % of reward time.
ideas.mechanism: Other makers widening is itself information: it is the visible half of a withdrawal decision, and it is observable in our context one event before the sweep it precedes. This is the mirror image of the jump rule - here the price has not moved yet, so the OFI gate sees nothing and the mid-based signals are silent, while the spread says the book's own risk premium just doubled. The general result that liquidity provision contracts ahead of informed trading (and that the race is between cancel and snipe) is exactly what a widening encodes. The counterparty is the informed taker who is about to cross a now-wide spread; our quote, if left inside it, is the cheapest thing to hit. Distinct from jump detection (no price move), from bounce (spread is not oscillating), and from depth imbalance (both sides moved).
ideas.data: DecisionContext only: spread_cents, tick_size, mid, best_bid, best_ask per update; the module keeps a 50-event deque of spread_cents and of mids. No derived table, no clock.

ideas.kill: Kill if the post-widening markout gap is below 0.3 c/share, or if widening episodes occur in fewer than 2 % of updates, or if reward forfeiture exceeds the markout saving on both slices.

ideas.title: Reward per dollar and cent-risk per dollar are both 1/price-shaped, until the tails break
ideas.claim: A share earns the same score and the same cent markout at any price, so reward per committed dollar and risk per committed dollar both scale as 1/price; if the measured per-share markout is price-flat the two cancel, but on this tape the extremes carry worse markout, so sizing proportional to 1 - |2*mid - 1| (full at 0.50, min size outside 0.20-0.80) improves net per committed dollar by >= 10 % versus constant-share sizing.
ideas.mechanism: The score counts shares, the fill cost is cents per share, and the inventory cap is shares, while capital is dollars - so at mid 0.05 the same share count buys a twentieth of the score-relevant capital but carries the same $0.01-per-share adverse move, i.e. 20 % of price. Prediction-market prices near the boundary are where the repo's own tape work finds the losing side of the favourite-longshot spread (20-30 % priced resolves 12.2 % in sports) and where a single news item reprices whole cents; the boundary is also where the venue requires strict two-sidedness, so the reward is not richer to compensate. The pool therefore pays the same per share in the tails while the counterparty is more informed there. This is grid-position sizing, not band eligibility and not a variance estimate.

ideas.kill: Kill if per-share markout is flat across the three price buckets (spread below 0.3 c/share), or if the paired net-per-dollar improvement is under 5 % on both slices, or if fewer than 50 conditions have a token outside 0.20-0.80.

ideas.title: Thin levels are sweep magnets, deep levels are not
ideas.claim: Fills taken on a side whose touch level size is in the bottom quartile of its own trailing distribution carry markout of -1.0 c/share or worse, versus -0.2 c/share or better in the top quartile, so shrinking the thin side (and never the deep one) improves paired net by >= $0.001/share at matched fill count.
ideas.mechanism: A print reaches our quote only after consuming the level ahead of it; when the displayed level is thin, one aggressive print clears several ticks and the fill is a sweep, while a deep level absorbs the same print within the level and the fill is noise. Depth is the barrier that decides whether the trade carries information, which is the same reason price impact scales inversely with depth in Cont, Kukanov & Stoikov (2014). The measured logistic here already says fill probability falls with level size (coefficient -0.5733 on log1p(size)); the claim is that the *conditional* markout rises faster than the probability falls, so exposure should be pulled from thin levels. This uses level depth, not our FIFO position, and not any price signal.

ideas.kill: Kill if the quartile markout gap is below 0.3 c/share, or if the bottom-quartile fills are not worse than -0.5 c/share, or if the paired net delta is negative on either slice.

ideas.title: The reward is linear in size, so size is a scaling decision and not a strategy
ideas.claim: Score is linear in size and in time-in-band, so reward dollars per unit of fill notional are invariant to the (size, presence) mix within 10 %; therefore min-size quoting with full presence leaves reward per notional unchanged, and since the baseline's own net per share is negative (-0.00628 $/share on 777 marked fills), cutting size to the qualifying floor improves paired net by >= $0.001/share without any signal.
ideas.mechanism: Q_epoch sums per-minute scores, each linear in size, so doubling size and halving presence is score-neutral; and Q_normal = Q_min/(Q_min + C) is concave in our own size, which makes *more samples at smaller size* weakly better than fewer at larger size for the same total. The cost side is not neutral: fill notional is what gets adversely selected, and the venue's min-size rule means the smallest qualifying order still scores. The pool therefore cannot make an unprofitable per-share book profitable by paying more per share, and the counterparty is paid by the same linearity. The test is an invariance check with a directional decision attached - if per-share net is scale-invariant, the only rational size is the floor.
ideas.data: DecisionContext only: inventory, queue ratios, sizes; rewards_min_size at setup. No derived table, no clock.
ideas.module: ideas.micro-time-vs-size.module
ideas.metric: Two numbers, both required: (a) reward_usd / fill_notional at min size versus at full size, which is the invariance check, and (b) paired per-condition net against reactionary, the deciding number. A violation of (a) beyond 10 % means the model is wrong, not that the strategy is good.
ideas.kill: Kill if reward_usd / fill_notional changes by more than 25 % between min and full size (the linearity assumption is false and every reward-sizing idea here needs rebasing), or if paired net is not positive on both slices, or if fills fall below the 200-fill / 50-condition gate.

ideas.kill_reason: Refuted by the capital sweep on the frozen slice: net rises from $35.19 to $88.76 as the per-market multiplier goes 0.10 to 1.00. Minimum size with full presence is the losing side of that trade-off here.

ideas.title: Q_min couples the two sides: a one-sided pull is a self-inflicted penalty
ideas.claim: Because Q_min = max(min(Q1,Q2), max(Q1,Q2)/3) inside mid 0.10-0.90 and min(Q1,Q2) outside it, a protective rule that pulls exactly one side loses at least two-thirds of that epoch's score for one side's worth of risk reduction; on tail-price conditions (mid < 0.10 or > 0.90) it loses all of it, so symmetric pull must beat per-side pull by >= $0.002/share net on those conditions.
ideas.mechanism: The venue scores our two book sides and takes the minimum: Q1 = YES bids + NO asks, Q2 = YES asks + NO bids, with a factor c = 3.0 for the single-sided case inside [0.10, 0.90] and a strict minimum outside it (Polymarket docs, eqs. 2-4). So dropping one side does not cost "half" the reward; it costs 2/3 of it in the band and 100 % of it in the tails, while the adverse-selection saving is one side's markout only. The pool underpays a hedged two-sided maker relative to what the maker's risk model assumes, and the mispricing is largest exactly where the engine's own inventory skew is least useful (prices near 0 or 1).
ideas.data: DecisionContext plus MarketView (rate_per_day, rewards_min_size, rewards_max_spread). No derived table; mid and the per-side queue ratios are in the context.
ideas.module: ideas.micro-two-sided-coupling.module
ideas.metric: Paired per-condition net and rewards_usd on tail conditions, plus the fraction of conditions where the two Q sides are simultaneously populated (a two-sidedness proxy the harness can compute from the per-token epoch snapshots); deciding number is the paired net difference against queue_aware_ofi. Caveat: paper_trading/rewards.compute_epoch_payout has no Q_min and no c = 3 penalty, so on today's engine a one-sided book is scored additively; the proxy, not rewards_usd, is the falsifying number until that scoring is patched.
ideas.kill: Kill if, on tail conditions, symmetric pull is worse than per-side pull by more than $0.002/share on both slices, or if fewer than 3 % of rewarded conditions sit outside [0.10, 0.90] at any point in the slice.

ideas.title: Quote size should scale with 1/variance, not with the pool
ideas.claim: Realized path variance computed from the mid alone separates good and bad quoting regimes: conditions in the top volatility tercile carry markout -1.5 c/share or worse while the bottom tercile is at least 0, so scaling both sides' size by min(1, (sigma_ref/sigma)^2) with sigma_ref set at the universe median improves paired net by >= $0.002/share.
ideas.mechanism: Avellaneda-Stoikov makes the optimal quote size and spread functions of sigma^2: the inventory term is q*gamma*sigma^2*(T-t), so the risk carried by a fixed share scales with variance while the reward for it does not (the score is variance-free). A maker who quotes the same size in a quiet and a violent condition is therefore mis-sizing by the ratio of their variances. This is not the jump or widening rule: no single event triggers it, and the same mid path can be smooth or violent with identical spreads. The counterparty in the violent tercile is the informed taker who is paid for exactly the size we over-supplied; in the quiet tercile we are under-supplied relative to what the pool pays.
ideas.data: DecisionContext only: successive book.mid values. The module computes sigma_hat = mean(|dmid|) over the last 100 changes * 100 (cents, time-free), plus a long-run reference from setup-time defaults. No derived table, no clock.

ideas.kill: Kill if the tercile markout ladder is flat (spread below 0.3 c/share), or if the applied scale is 1.0 or the floor for more than 90 % of updates (the signal does not vary), or if paired net is not positive on both slices.

ideas.claim: A market whose own realised P&L per fill is negative after at least 8 fills is not paying for the reward it earns; withdrawing improves paired net on the withdrawn subset without hurting the kept one.
ideas.mechanism: Reward is payment for resting, adverse selection is the price; which dominates is market-specific and only visible in our own fills, so the rule is adaptive and per market.

ideas.kill: Kill if fewer than 20 conditions are withdrawn, or if the kept subset loses more than the withdrawn subset gains.
